Subject: Split-jurisdiction proposal and emergency relief carveout — MSA/Order Form

Team / Liz —

Thanks for the helpful redlines on the MSA. Crestline pushed back on our carveout for injunctive relief and is proposing an arbitration-only route with a single seat. Before we get into a back-and-forth, I want to propose a compromise that preserves our ability to obtain urgent injunctive relief (for IP, data exfiltration, or immediate order-stopping scenarios) while keeping most disputes in arbitration. High-level proposal:

- Governing law: New York law (familiar commercial body of law for our ops).
- Seat/administration: Arbitration for monetary and merits disputes administered by AAA (or ICC if customer prefers) with a neutral seat (London or New York) to be negotiated.
- Carveout for interim relief: Notwithstanding arbitration, permit either party to seek temporary injunctive or preservative relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm. Any such action should be limited to interim measures and not decide merits; the parties will promptly refer the dispute to arbitration for final determination.

Key asks:
1) Liz — is the language above workable from an enforcement perspective? Does 'any court of competent jurisdiction' create a risk we can't defend later in arbitration?
2) Carlos — can your team accept New York law as governing while we keep a neutral seat for arbitration?
3) Internal — can Risk/Compliance confirm if we need specific wording around data-related emergency relief (e.g., ability to obtain an order to preserve logs/data in-situ)?

I've attached the current MSA_redline_v4.docx and the OrderForm so legal can propose redline snippets. If we can get a short agreed clause by EOD Friday (2 May), we can push the combined redline back to Crestline next week.

Thanks —

Naomi / team —

Thanks for the summary. Short answers first: yes, we can craft a clause that preserves our ability to seek interim injunctive relief without voiding the arbitration agreement, but the precise wording matters to minimize forum-shopping risk. A few considerations:

- "Any court of competent jurisdiction" is broad; it gives flexibility but could invite tactical filings in multiple jurisdictions. If we want to limit exposure while keeping speed, we can use: "any court of competent jurisdiction where the subject matter or relevant assets are located".
- Split seat (governing law NY; arbitration seat London) is workable but adds complexity if enforcement is in different jurisdictions — better to pick a seat that both sides see as neutral.
- To protect enforcement of interim measures, include a clause requiring the party seeking interim relief to provide notice to the arbitral tribunal (if constituted) and to promptly seek consolidation of remedies when possible.

Suggested snippet (draft redline):
"Notwithstanding the parties' agreement to resolve disputes through arbitration, either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief from any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm. Any such request for provisional relief shall be without prejudice to the right of the party to refer the dispute to arbitration for a final determination, and the tribunal shall retain jurisdiction to determine the merits of any claim subsequently referred to arbitration. The party seeking provisional relief shall, where reasonably practicable, notify the other party and the arbitral tribunal of the action and shall cooperate to avoid duplicative proceedings."

Data note: For data-preservation orders, include explicit language allowing preservation of logs and backups for a defined period (e.g., 30 days) and require a narrowly tailored preservation request.

If you want, I can produce a tracked-change version of the MSA with the above inserted and a short memo on enforcement risk by EOD Thursday.

Cheers,

Thanks everyone — quick mutual action plan and next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

1) Legal (Liz/Redwood Legal) — produce tracked MSA with the proposed carveout language + two alternative wordings (narrow and broad) by EOD Monday, 5 May. (Liz offered a draft; please include Karthik's expedited-arbitration threshold language.)
2) Ops (Irene) — confirm whether our onboarding/data team can commit to 24-hour acknowledgment and preservation steps for emergency requests; identify two escalation contacts (legal + infra) and share by COB Monday.
3) Commercial (Marissa / Karthik) — confirm whether Crestline can accept NY governing law or wants Delaware; if customer insists on a single-seat arbitration, capture their seat preference so legal can model enforcement.
4) Risk/Compliance — advise if we need additional data-specific preservation wording (e.g., scope of retained logs, retention window).

Proposed short clause to insert (we'll let legal refine):
"Interim Relief: Notwithstanding Section X (Arbitration), either party may apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for interim or conservatory measures, including injunctive relief and orders to preserve data. Such application shall be without prejudice to the requirement to submit the dispute to arbitration, and the requesting party shall, where practicable, notify the arbitral tribunal and the other party. The parties agree to use reasonable efforts to coordinate provisional measures with the arbitral process to minimize duplicative proceedings."

If we can get the tracked changes on Monday, I'll schedule a short patch-call with Crestline next Tuesday to resolve seat/governing-law. 

Naomi
